sections.skill: Compare mutual funds, ETFs, and index funds and explain how they are priced

questions.domain: Investing, Brokerage Accounts, and Investment Products
questions.prompt: What is a mutual fund?

choices.text: A pool of investors' money that buys many securities
A single company's stock sold at a discount
An FDIC-insured savings product at a bank
A loan that a group of friends makes together to one person

questions.correct_answer: A pool of investors' money that buys many securities
questions.intro: A mutual fund pools money from many investors to buy a collection (portfolio) of stocks, bonds, or other securities, managed by professionals. Each investor owns shares of the fund. Mutual fund shares are bought and sold once a day at the net asset value (NAV) calculated after the market closes.
questions.feedback: A mutual fund pools money to buy many securities.
questions.topic: Mutual funds, ETFs, and index funds

misconceptions.B: Confuses a fund with one stock

sources: SEC Investor.gov: Mutual funds are priced once a day at net asset value; ETF shares trade on exchanges throughout the day at market prices. (https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/investment-products/mutual-funds-and-exchange-traded-funds-etfs)

questions.domain: Investing, Brokerage Accounts, and Investment Products
questions.prompt: How is an ETF (exchange-traded fund) different from a traditional mutual fund?

choices.text: ETFs can hold only one stock at a time
ETFs are insured by the FDIC
ETFs are bought only once a year at one fixed price
ETF shares trade on an exchange throughout the day

questions.correct_answer: ETF shares trade on an exchange throughout the day
questions.intro: An ETF also holds a basket of securities, but its shares trade on stock exchanges throughout the day at market prices, like stocks. Traditional mutual funds trade once a day at NAV.
questions.feedback: ETFs trade all day like stocks; mutual funds price once a day.
questions.topic: Mutual funds, ETFs, and index funds
sources: SEC Investor.gov: Mutual funds are priced once a day at net asset value; ETF shares trade on exchanges throughout the day at market prices. (https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/investment-products/mutual-funds-and-exchange-traded-funds-etfs)

questions.domain: Investing, Brokerage Accounts, and Investment Products
questions.prompt: What does an S&P 500 index fund try to do?

choices.text: Beat the S&P 500 by picking winning stocks each week
Guarantee a 5% return every year
Hold only the 5 largest companies
Match the performance of the S&P 500 index

questions.correct_answer: Match the performance of the S&P 500 index
questions.intro: An index is a list that measures part of the market; the S&P 500 tracks about 500 large U.S. companies. An index fund (a mutual fund or ETF) holds the securities in an index to match its performance, not to beat it. Index funds usually have low costs.
questions.feedback: Index funds aim to match an index, typically at low cost.
questions.topic: Mutual funds, ETFs, and index funds
sources: SEC Investor.gov: Mutual funds are priced once a day at net asset value; ETF shares trade on exchanges throughout the day at market prices. (https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/investment-products/mutual-funds-and-exchange-traded-funds-etfs)

questions.domain: Investing, Brokerage Accounts, and Investment Products
questions.prompt: A fund has $50,000,000 in assets, $500,000 in liabilities, and 2,000,000 shares outstanding. What is its NAV per share?
questions.intro: Net asset value per share = (total assets − total liabilities) ÷ shares outstanding.
questions.topic: Mutual funds, ETFs, and index funds

questions.domain: Investing, Brokerage Accounts, and Investment Products
questions.prompt: A fund holds 400 different stocks. If one stock falls 50%, why does the fund fall much less?

choices.text: The fund refunds the loss
That stock is only a small part of the fund
Funds sell any stock before it falls
The other 399 stocks in it must all rise by 50%

questions.correct_answer: That stock is only a small part of the fund
questions.intro: In a fund, each holding is a small part of the whole, so one holding's drop has a small effect.
questions.feedback: Each holding is a small slice, so one drop moves the fund only a little.
questions.topic: Mutual funds, ETFs, and index funds

misconceptions.C: Believes managers can always avoid drops

questions.prompt: An actively managed fund charges 0.80% a year; an index fund tracking a similar market charges 0.05%. On $10,000, how much more does the active fund cost per year?
questions.intro: Active funds try to beat the market by choosing investments; they usually cost more. Passive (index) funds try to match the market at low cost.

questions.prompt: What does "passive" investing mean?

choices.text: Holding an index fund instead of trying to pick winners
Never checking your account again
Investing only in savings accounts
Letting a friend choose your stocks

questions.correct_answer: Holding an index fund instead of trying to pick winners
questions.intro: Passive investing aims to match the market's return by owning the whole index, rather than predicting which stocks will do best.
questions.feedback: Passive investing tracks a market index.

questions.prompt: Two S&P 500 index funds track the same index. Fund A charges 0.03%; Fund B charges 0.50%. Which is generally the better choice?

choices.text: Fund B, because higher fees mean better management
Either, because fees never matter
Fund A, because the holdings are nearly identical and it costs less
Fund B, because a higher fee means better management

questions.correct_answer: Fund A, because the holdings are nearly identical and it costs less
questions.intro: When two funds hold nearly the same investments, the lower-cost fund usually leaves more of the return for the investor.
questions.feedback: For funds that track the same index, lower cost usually wins.
